sources.fact: Keystore can keep keys non-exportable; hardware placement and supported authorizations depend on the actual key/device. Secure hardware normally does not enforce calendar validity because an independent secure real-time clock is generally absent.
API31 provides limited-use secret/private keys. Enforcement can be software or hardware; dedicated PackageManager features report hardware single/limited-use support.
KeyMint rollback resistance specifically prevents reuse of a deleted key even if an attacker restores an earlier keyblob; trusted metadata may be resource-limited.

inferences.detail: A hardware-backed key or limited-use feature alone is not evidence that the current full-record digest, native action consumption and signed epoch-anchor contract have been implemented and verified. A ratchet or checkpoint design would need an exact supported API guarantee, failure recovery and installed-device evidence before it could replace the null native factory.

remainingCodexWork: Implement and validate an exact supported checkpoint/action provider and native coordinator; do not transfer programming to the owner.
Implement authenticated epoch-anchor provenance and restart handling; do not substitute Date.now or an ordinary stored checksum.
Keep child mode sealed until protected admission and lifecycle/route wiring are actually complete.
